item.title: Renault CEO sees strong hybrids matching CNG's market share in India
item.description: Stephane Deblaise expects strong hybrids to gain ground as Renault expands its SUV portfolio, introduces new powertrains and targets double-digit annual sales growth ...
item.dc:creator: Deepak Patel
item.content:encoded: Renault Group India expects strong hybrid vehicles to eventually command at least the same share of India's passenger vehicle market as compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered cars, as the former offer lower fuel consumption and emissions without the need for external charging, its chief executive officer (CEO), Stephane Deblaise, said on Sunday. “I don't see how a country such as India can avoid having a big number of strong hybrids,” he said, adding that hybrids allow customers to enjoy an electric driving experience without the charging constraints of battery electric vehicles (BEVs). He also said Renault would welcome greater government incentives for strong hybrids to encourage their adoption and reduce emissions. CNG-powered vehicles accounted for 25.28 per cent of India's passenger vehicle retail sales in August 2026, up from 21.47 per cent a year earlier, according to data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada). Hybrids, including mild and strong hybrids, accounted for 9.04 per cent of sales in August, up from 7.96 per cent a year earlier. A separate analysis of Vahan registration data puts the combined share of strong hybrids and plug-in hybrids at around 2 per cent of passenger vehicle retail sales in 2025-26. Asked whether strong hybrids could gain a significantly larger share of India's passenger vehicle market than electric vehicles over the next two to three years, Deblaise said their growth would depend partly on how many automakers introduced the technology and the kind of tax incentives available. He said he expected hybrids to eventually account for at least as much of the market as CNG vehicles. “Big amount, I don't know how much it will reach, but... it would be at least the same level as CNG,” he said. Renault on Saturday launched the Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160, marking the introduction of its strong-hybrid powertrain in India. The company has announced an Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI)-certified fuel efficiency of 29 km per litre for the SUV. “If the intention really is to have better health of the population and lower carbon dioxide emissions, it makes sense to push strong hybrids,” he said. Beyond the hybrid launch, Renault is preparing nearly 10 major product and powertrain events over the next 12 months, Deblaise said. The company plans to introduce new engines and gearboxes, add CNG options to the Triber and Kiger, and expand its range towards larger sport utility vehicles (SUVs) and more electrified vehicles. It is also considering the introduction of a BEV in 2027 or 2028.“Every year we will sell much more cars than the year before. We expect to see two digit growth,” Deblaise said, while declining to disclose absolute sales targets for the coming years. He said Renault wanted to build steady growth rather than achieve a strong year followed by a weak one, adding that the company would not push sales artificially to meet a particular market-share target. The turnaround strategy involves moving beyond Renault's traditional entry-level positioning. The company has so far relied on the Kwid, Triber and Kiger, but is now looking to expand into higher-priced segments through the Duster, the upcoming Bridger and a larger seven-seater SUV. “Until now, we had only one platform,” Deblaise said, referring to the CMFA architecture underpinning its entry-level models.Renault now has two platforms: the Renault Group Entry Platform (RGEP), an updated version of CMFA intended to support new technology and a wider range of powertrains, including CNG, and the Renault Group Medium Platform (RGMP), introduced with the Duster and intended for hybrid and other electrified vehicles. The shift is expected to move Renault from vehicles priced around ₹7 lakh towards products priced around ₹16 lakh. Deblaise said the challenge was not just to introduce new models but to provide better value and attract customers in segments where Renault has had a limited presence. The company is also reviewing its dealership network, with a focus on improving customer experience rather than significantly increasing the number of outlets. The exercise began around 18 months ago and involves assessing locations, upgrading facilities, relocating some dealerships and closing poorly located ones.The cost of improvements can range from ₹25 lakh for limited work to ₹1.25 crore for more extensive refurbishment, Deblaise said. He added that digital upgrades alone could cost around ₹25 lakh, while a light refurbishment could cost about ₹50 lakh and more extensive work around ₹1 crore. Renault hopes to complete the main push by the end of 2027, although Deblaise described dealership improvement as an ongoing process. The company is also investing in salesperson training and retention. “We will increase our dealers a little bit, but not a lot. This is not our main intention. Our main intention is to make it better,” he said. Deblaise also identified the ₹9 lakh-₹15 lakh price band as a significant opportunity for the company. He estimated that the segment accounts for more than 1 million vehicles and said sales of cars priced above ₹10 lakh had increased by around 40 per cent over the past five years.

item.title: Zelenskyy criticizes Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong'
item.description: Zelenskyy criticised US President Donald Trump's decision to waive Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, saying the move would encourage Moscow to continue attacks on Ukraine ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Zelenskyy criticizes Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong'

Zelenskyy criticizes Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong' Zelenskyy criticised US President Donald Trump's decision to waive Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, saying the move would encourage Moscow to continue attacks on Ukraine

Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters WASHINGTON 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 18 2026 | 8:09 AM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on its goods days before they were to take effect will embolden Moscow to keep attacking Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday, predicting even more US sanctions relief.   "The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskyy wrote on X. "It definitely helps only the Russians."   An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs - including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas - that had been scheduled to start next week under the legislation known as the Graham Act that he signed into law last month.

Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the United States.   The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticizing Zelenskyy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader. Also Read

Trump wants 60 days to analyse impact of Russia sanctions law: Rubio

India to keep Russian oil imports near current levels after Trump waiver

Trump's sanctions waiver offers India temporary relief, no certainty: GTRI

Saudi Arabia should accept Israel's 'helpful' offer to fight Houthis: Trump

Trump waives Russia energy tariffs and sanctions under Graham law

Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin.   "It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskyy, who said Russia struck more than 15 Ukrainian power generation and transmission sites on Friday. "This certainly does not stop the war."   The Ukrainian leader accused Russia of planning to ramp up strikes in western Ukraine. "Is Russia preparing for this? I think so," Zelenskyy wrote.

RUSSIAN ENVOY PRAISES WAIVER   Russia's investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, called the Trump waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X on Friday that had the penalties taken effect, they could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt.   Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further raising oil prices as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war with Iran, analysts have said.   Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September.

The legislation's primary backer in Congress was the late US Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican. It would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions.   Graham's sister, Darline Graham, was appointed to fill his Senate seat after he died in July, and Trump endorsed her for a full term heading into the midterm elections. At a campaign stop on Saturday, she did not directly criticize Trump for waiving sanctions, but she said she would not have made that choice.

"Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia," she told reporters, according to multiple news outlets. "Because I don't trust Putin and I don't trust Russia."   China and India, which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, however, had raised concerns about the Graham Act.   Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties.   But the Graham Act also allows the president to waive sanctions by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest. Friday's executive order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate."

US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, said Trump was giving in to Putin.   "Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement on Friday.   Lindsey Graham, who died in July, strongly supported US assistance to Ukraine. The passage of the bill named for him had provided hope of continued bipartisan support for Kyiv, wrote Zelenskyy.   But with Graham gone, the US under Trump will continue sanctions relief for Russia beyond Friday's waiver and the diesel export agreement announced earlier this month, the Ukrainian leader predicted.

"I think the diesel deal and the move regarding the Lindsey Graham Act are not the end of it. Unfortunately," wrote Zelenskyy, who lamented Graham's absence. "It's unfortunate because we all had great respect for Lindsey … It's difficult without him, I'll be honest."

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Serious incident caused major fire at military base in Alberta: Canada's PM
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that a "serious incident" caused a major fire at a military base in Alberta.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Serious incident caused major fire at military base in Alberta: Canada's PM

Serious incident caused major fire at military base in Alberta: Canada's PM The cause of the fire and whether anyone was injured remain unclear

Carney said the federal government was working closely with Alberta officials and local authorities | Image: Bloomberg

AP Edmonton 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 18 2026 | 7:47 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that a "serious incident" caused a major fire at a military base in Alberta. "A serious incident creating a major fire has occurred at CFB Wainwright, in Alberta," Carney said on Saturday in a social media post. "Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected," he said. Carney said the federal government was working closely with Alberta officials and local authorities. He said he and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith were in close contact, as were their ministers and officials. Carney did not provide details about what caused the fire or whether anyone was injured.
